subject.title: fix(codex): user-home Codex app-servers fail every turn when an OpenAI auth profile exists

question: Should this auth-routing change merge after a redacted real user-home Codex app-server run proves that stored OpenAI profiles are not injected and turns complete on the native Codex account?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes credential-routing behavior for a home shared with Codex CLI/Desktop; unit and harness tests establish intended control flow but cannot demonstrate the real app-server/account interaction required by the repository proof policy.

options.title: Require real user-home proof
options.body: Request a redacted after-fix run with `homeScope: "user"`, a stored OpenAI profile, and supervision enabled, showing a completed turn without prepared-auth injection.

options.title: Pause for owner validation
options.body: Hold the PR until the Codex-area owner confirms the native-account verification behavior against the current Codex app-server contract.

recommendation.title: Require real user-home proof
recommendation.body: Request a redacted after-fix run with `homeScope: "user"`, a stored OpenAI profile, and supervision enabled, showing a completed turn without prepared-auth injection.

likelyOwner.reason: The available commit provenance shows direct ownership of the proposed app-server auth routing and regression coverage.
